title: The Elite Backend Engineer
subtitle: A day-by-day roadmap from beginner to elite backend engineer — same 13 phases as the original plan, expanded in full depth with nothing skipped

meta.daily_commitment: 2-3 focused hours (dense days may bleed into the next day)
meta.starting_point: Comfortable with basic CRUD apps in Java
meta.end_state: Production-grade distributed systems capstone + interview-ready depth across DSA, system design, and backend engineering
meta.dsa_habit_note: Starting immediately after the DSA phase ends, keep solving one DSA problem a day as a standing habit for the rest of the roadmap, in addition to that day's listed topic.
ground_rules: Write code every day. Reading about a topic without typing it out doesn't count.
Commit to GitHub daily, even small progress.
Keep a running technical journal: after each day, write 3-5 sentences explaining the concept in your own words (Feynman technique). If you can't explain it simply, you don't know it yet.
2-3 hrs/day is the target, not a ceiling. If a day's topic is dense, let it bleed into the next day rather than rushing.
Every 'Checkpoint' day is non-negotiable. That's where scattered knowledge becomes a system you can defend under questioning.
This calendar assumes roughly 6 days/week with occasional slack — treat the total as elapsed calendar time, not a rigid sprint.
before_day_1_setup: Install JDK 21 (LTS) and confirm with java -version.
Install IntelliJ IDEA (Community is fine to start).
Install PostgreSQL locally (or via Docker) and a client such as DBeaver.
Install Postman or use IntelliJ's HTTP client for API testing.
Create a dedicated GitHub repo (or one per phase) to track daily commits.
